questions.enonce_markdown:
**Translate into French**

> One bright day, Mrs Aïshatou, an old woman, was sitting alone in her house. She had lost her husband and was living all alone. She had been sick the whole week but didn't have money to go to the hospital. There was no one to prepare food and fetch water for her. She was weak and hungry. She had spent the whole day thinking of her late husband. She wished she could also die soon.

> A few minutes later, someone knocked at the door. Mrs. Aïshatou got up from bed and shouted:

> "Thank you, Lord, for answering my prayers. Take me to my husband."

> When she opened the door, she saw a young beautiful woman who was smiling.

> "Mrs. Aïshatou," Fadi said, "I am the little girl you helped many years ago. I have come to take you."

> Suddenly, Mrs. Aïshatou's life changed. Fadi who had become a doctor took her to live with her.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model translation**

Un beau jour, Mme Aïshatou, une vieille femme, était assise seule dans sa maison. Elle avait perdu son mari et vivait toute seule. Elle était malade depuis toute la semaine, mais elle n'avait pas d'argent pour aller à l'hôpital. Il n'y avait personne pour lui préparer à manger et lui chercher de l'eau. Elle était faible et affamée. Elle avait passé toute la journée à penser à son défunt mari. Elle souhaitait pouvoir mourir bientôt, elle aussi.

Quelques minutes plus tard, quelqu'un frappa à la porte. Mme Aïshatou se leva de son lit et cria :

« Merci, Seigneur, d'avoir exaucé mes prières. Emmène-moi auprès de mon mari. »

Quand elle ouvrit la porte, elle vit une belle jeune femme qui souriait.

« Madame Aïshatou, dit Fadi, je suis la petite fille que vous avez aidée il y a de nombreuses années. Je suis venue vous chercher. »

Soudain, la vie de Mme Aïshatou changea. Fadi, qui était devenue médecin, l'emmena vivre chez elle.

**Translation points**

| Point | Trap | Correct form |
|---|---|---|
| Setting the scene in the past | Using the passé composé for a description | Imparfait for states and ongoing actions: *était assise*, *vivait*, *était faible* |
| "She had lost", "she had spent" | Using the simple past or the imparfait | Plus-que-parfait for what happened before the scene: *avait perdu*, *avait passé* |
| "had been sick the whole week" | Translating "for" with *pour* | *malade depuis toute la semaine* (the illness began earlier and is still true in the scene; *avait été malade toute la semaine* is also accepted) |
| "didn't have money to go to the hospital" | Keeping the article: *pas un argent* | After a negation, *pas d'argent*; *aller à l'hôpital* |
| "There was no one to prepare food" | Word for word: *il y avait pas de personne* | *Il n'y avait personne pour lui préparer à manger* (negation *ne ... personne*, indirect object pronoun *lui*) |
| "her late husband" | *son tard mari* | *son défunt mari* |
| "knocked", "got up", "shouted", "opened", "saw" | Mixing imparfait, passé simple and passé composé without a reason | A series of single, completed actions: passé simple (*frappa, se leva, cria, ouvrit, vit*) or passé composé throughout |
| "Thank you, Lord, for answering my prayers" | *pour répondre à mes prières* | *Merci, Seigneur, d'avoir exaucé mes prières* (*merci de* + past infinitive, because the answer came before the thanks) |
| "a young beautiful woman" | *une jeune belle femme* | *une belle jeune femme* (*une jeune et belle femme* is also correct) |
| "the little girl you helped many years ago" | *que vous avez aidé* (no agreement); *depuis* for "ago" | Agreement with the preceding direct object: *que vous avez aidée*; "ago" = *il y a de nombreuses années* |
| "who had become a doctor" | *qui avait devenu*; *un docteur* with an article | *qui était devenue médecin* (*devenir* takes *être*; feminine agreement; no article before a profession) |
| "took her to live with her" | *avec elle* repeated mechanically | *l'emmena vivre chez elle* |

**Marking note**

The text is short, so every sentence counts. Credit goes to accuracy (tenses, agreements, accents) and to natural French rather than word-for-word translation. Keep the quotation marks and the punctuation of the direct speech.

**Common mistakes**

1. Leaving out a sentence or part of a sentence (for example "She wished she could also die soon"). Everything in the source must be translated.
2. Using one tense for the whole text. The scene is described in the imparfait and plus-que-parfait, while the events are in the passé simple or passé composé.
